topics.description: An Athenian lawgiver whose reforms replaced much of Draco’s harsh code and helped lay the foundations of Athenian democracy.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: This city’s Alcmaeonid family got themselves cursed and exiled until Hippias was overthrown by  Cleisthenes. A harsh law code in this city, which included a death penalty for stealing cabbages, was written  by Draco, and almost entirely replaced by (*) Solon. This city led the Delian League, and embezzled funds from  it to fund the Parthenon. For 10 points, name this birthplace of democracy in Ancient Greece.

topics.description: An Ottoman sultan who expanded the empire into the Balkans, completed the conquest of Bulgaria, and was captured by Timur at Ankara in 1402.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Items such as an entire Quran inscribed within a ring were produced during this conqueror's  namesake “Renaissance.” For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this Uzbek (OOZ-bek) warlord who, from his capital of Samarkand (SAA-mark-and),  assembled an empire stretching from Delhi to Damascus in the late 14th century.
parts.answer: Tamerlane (TAM-er-lain) [or Tamerlame; or Timur the Lame; or Timūr Gurkānī; or  Temür Küregen]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] An eleven-year “Interregnum” in this Turkish Islamic empire began in 1402 after Timur captured  its sultan at the Battle of Ankara (ONK-uh-ruh).

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Timur captured this Ottoman sultan at Ankara. This sultan, who took the throne after Murad I's  death at the Battle of Kosovo (KAW-suh-voh), completed the Ottoman conquest of Bulgaria at Nicopolis  (nik-AH-puh-lis) in 1396.
parts.answer: Bayezid (bai-EZ-id) the Thunderbolt [or Bayezid I; or Yıldırım Bayezid]

topics.description: Brexit was the United Kingdom’s withdrawal from the European Union, completed in 2020 after the 2016 membership referendum.
aliases: United Kingdom withdrawal from the European Union

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a speech where he made car noises, this politician complained about how Daddy Pig holds a negative stereotype. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [M] Name this politician, who resigned as prime minister of the U.K. in 2022. This politician is often referred to as “BoJo”.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] During the 2019 General Election, Boris Johnson ran on the slogan “Get [this action] done.” This term refers to Britain leaving the European Union in 2020.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [H] This politician, who resigned over Brexit, attacked Johnson and the Partygate scandal in a speech after he announced his resignation. Johnson succeeded this woman as prime minister.

topics.description: France’s national holiday, observed on July 14 to commemorate the 1789 storming of the Bastille and the beginning of the French Revolution.

parts.label: L
parts.question: This politician called the laissez-faire policies of John Major “Anglo-Saxon ultraliberalism.” For 10  points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this two-time prime minister who became president of France from 1995 to 2007. For his  second term, he founded the new UMP party.

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Chirac survived an assassination attempt in 2002 during this holiday, which commemorates the  storming of a Parisian prison that began the French Revolution on July 14, 1789.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Chirac commissioned a Bible scholar to write a briefing on Gog and Magog after being puzzled by  a metaphor in a 2003 phone call from the U.S. President arguing for this goal.
parts.answer: getting France to join in the U.S.-led coalition for the Iraq War [or answers referring to the  2003 Iraq War; or invasion of Iraq; or overthrow of Saddam Hussein]

topics.description: Jawaharlal Nehru was the first prime minister of independent India and a leading figure in the Indian independence movement.

parts.label: L
parts.question: In a speech after an attack by Nathuram Godse, this politician declared “friends and comrades, the light has gone out of our lives.” For ten points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [H] Name this politician, who not even a year earlier gave his inaugural address titled “Tryst with Destiny.” This politician was the first prime minister of a newly independent India.
parts.answer: Jawaharlal Nehru [accept Pandit Nehru or Chacha Nehru]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [E] This was the surname of Nehru’s daughter, the first female Prime Minister of India. This was also the surname of a political leader who led nonviolent protests against British rule over India and was given the title Mahatma.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [M] During her time as Prime Minister, Indira Gandhi went to war with this country in support of Bangladesh’s independence. On the other hand, Mahatma Gandhi was against separation of India and this western neighbor.
parts.answer: Pakistan [or Islamic Republic of Pakistan or Jamhuryat Islami Pakistan]

topics.description: A major political and social conflict in Canada over compulsory military service during the First World War.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: A holder of this position declared that “the twentieth century belongs to [his country].” A constitutional crisis ensued when one holder of this position was replaced by Arthur Meighen in the King-Byng affair. A different holder of this position faced the Conscription Crisis during the First World War. The Pacific Scandal resulted in the resignation of the first holder of this position, (*) John MacDonald. Later holders of this position included William Lyon Mackenzie King and Pierre Trudeau. For 10 points, name this office whose holder oversees a government based in Ottawa.
parts.answer: Prime Minister of Canada [prompt on Prime Minister by asking “of what country?”; do NOT accept or prompt on “President of Canada”]

topics.description: The 1933 burning of Germany’s Reichstag, which the Nazis used to justify repression of communists and consolidate power through the Enabling Act.

parts.label: L
parts.question: Members of this political party reportedly claimed “After Hitler, our turn,” because they believed Hitler’s reign as chancellor would be short-lived. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: Name this political party that was led in the 1932 German elections by Ernst Thalmann. This party was founded by the leader of the Spartacist revolt, Rosa Luxemburg.

parts.label: B
parts.question: The Communists lost the elections of 1932 to this far-right political party, which was led by Adolf Hitler. This party carried out the Holocaust and was in power until Germany’s defeat in World War II.
parts.answer: Nazi Party [or National Socialist German Worker’s Party or Nationalsozialistische Deutsche Arbeiterpartei]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Hitler and the Nazis were able to consolidate political power after this event through the Enabling Act. This event was blamed on a Dutch communist, resulting in the arrest of the entire Communist parliamentary delegation.
parts.answer: Reichstag fire [or Reichstagsbrand; accept any answers indicating the burning of the Reichstag]

topics.description: The present-day Ukrainian city that served as the center of Kievan Rus, the medieval polity from which the name Rus originated.

parts.label: L
parts.question: The classroom doodlings of the boy Onfim (OHN-feem) were excavated in this city, which was the  site of a 1570 massacre ordered by Ivan (ee-VAHN) the Terrible. For 10 points each:

parts.label: A
parts.question: [10] Name this former Hanseatic (HAN-zee-AH-tik) city whose namesake northern republic, controlled  by the elected veche (vee-ETCH-eh), was the last major competitor to Moscow in Russia.
parts.answer: ANSWER: Novgorod (NAHV-guh-rod) [or Veliky Novgorod; do not accept or prompt on “Nizhny  Novgorod”]

parts.label: B
parts.question: [10] Novgorod was founded by the Varangian (vaa-RAN-ghee-un) prince Rurik, whose son Oleg  founded this other Rus (ROOS) city. The original Rus state was named for this now-Ukrainian city.

parts.label: C
parts.question: [10] Alexander Nevsky, a 13th-century prince of Novgorod, defeated this crusading order of German  speakers at the Battle on the Ice in 1242.

topics.description: A Portuguese explorer who rounded the southern tip of Africa in 1488, opening the sea route toward the Indian Ocean.

parts.label: L
parts.question: For ten points each, answer the following questions about Bartholomeu Dias.

parts.label: A
parts.question: Dias was an explorer for this country, for whom he sailed to regions such as modern day Namibia and Angola. Another explorer from this country, Pedro Cabral, was the European discoverer of Brazil.

parts.label: B
parts.question: On his way back from a voyage, Dias discovered and rounded this cape on the southern tip of Africa. Dias gave this cape the name “Cape of Storms,” though John II later gave it a more optimistic name.
parts.answer: Cape of Good Hope [prompt on the Cape]

parts.label: C
parts.question: Though Dias wanted to continue his voyage to the Indian Ocean, his crewmates unanimously voted to return to Portugal. This explorer later completed the full voyage, becoming the first European to reach India by sea.

topics.description: A system of French defensive fortifications along the eastern frontier that German forces bypassed during the 1940 invasion.

parts.label: tossup
parts.question: The launch of this military campaign ended an eight-month period of relative inaction dubbed  the “Phony War.” Maxime Weygand's (max-EEM VAY-gah's) planned counterattack failed to stop  this campaign. The Second Armistice at Compiègne (kahm-PEN-yeh) was signed just six weeks  after the start of this campaign, which took a route through the (*) Ardennes (ARD-en) Forest that  bypassed the Maginot (MAA-jin-oh) Line and led to the creation of the Vichy (VEE-shee) government.  For 10 points, name this World War II Nazi-led campaign whose outcome forced Charles de Gaulle  (SHARL day GOAL) to flee to Britain.
parts.answer: Battle of France [or German invasion of France; or Axis defeat of France in World War  II; or Nazi invasion of France until “Nazi” is read]
